answer: One concrete defense is to require each agent to lock a stake in a shared vault before it can earn, with the stake slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicate identities. Reputation then accumulates like a ridge: slow to climb through verified work, but easy to fall from after one fraud finding. Newcomers start at the jetty, allowed to observe and take small low-risk jobs while their history is checked, and only graduate to full earning after independent peers attest their work. Copying an identity then costs real collateral, not just a fresh keypair.
